title: Heatmap pruning and trace quota handoff — Observability sync
content:
Attendees: Evan Park (owner), Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Ritika Sharma, Marcus Lee, Lauren Chu (guest)

Meeting purpose
- Align on a short plan to reduce dashboard/heatmap cardinality, hand off a trace quota adjustment to the platform team, and update the tracing runbook before next release.

High-level context
- Datadog heatmap tiles and a handful of custom Grafana panels are top contributors to dashboard query cost (spike noted during last spike window 2026-09-12).
- Recent tenant onboarding increased tag cardinality on request.route and model.version which drove a 28% increase in heatmap query CPU time.
- Platform is ready to accept a temporary trace ingestion quota change for a controlled canary; we need to define scope and rollback criteria.

Agenda
1) Inventory: which heatmaps/panels are high-cost
2) Pruning plan: quick wins vs medium-term refactor
3) Trace quota handoff: scope, metrics, rollback
4) Runbook updates and action items

Notes
Inventory
- Current candidates for pruning (metrics from dashboard-inventory csv):
  - requests/latency/heatmap-by-route (top offender, high cardinality on route+model)
  - cpu/worker/hotspots-heatmap (replicated across three dashboards)
  - user-session-latency-heatmap (legacy, rarely referenced in last 90d)
- Owner recon: Marcus will run a quick query to confirm last-90d panel hit counts and list of teams referencing each panel (by 2026-09-20).

Pruning plan (30–60 day)
- Quick wins (apply within 1 week):
  - Hide user-session-latency-heatmap from global dashboards and move to archive dashboard folder (Sofia, due 2026-09-24).
  - Reduce resolution for 'cpu/worker/hotspots-heatmap' from per-1s to per-10s for tiles older than 24h (Liam, prod PR #482, target 2026-09-22).
  - Replace route+model multi-dimensional heatmap with two separate single-dim views (route heatmap + model histogram) to drop cross-product cardinality (Evan, design notes linked).
- Medium-term (30–60d):
  - Replace heavy heatmaps with pre-aggregated percentile endpoints (P50/P95/P99) served from ClickHouse materialized views.
  - Add dashboard access logs (if not present) to measure active usage monthly and auto-archive panels below threshold.

Trace quota handoff
- Request: platform to accept a temporary 10% reduction in global tracing ingestion (ingestion token: TRQ-2026-09) but allow 2% burst for emergencies.
- Scope: only spans with service in [api-gateway, frontend-proxy] and tag sampling applied by route (explicit whitelist for canary routes: /api/chat, /api/embeddings).
- Success metrics (canary window = 48h):
  - No increase >5% in 95th percentile tail latency for api-gateway requests.
  - No increase in 5xx rate >0.5% absolute.
  - Trace coverage for canary routes remains >= 70% of baseline for those routes.
- Rollback triggers (immediate rollback):
  - Alert: api-gateway.p95 latency increase >10% for 10m
  - Alert: error-rate increase >1% absolute for 10m
  - Manual abort requested by SRE on-duty
- Platform tasks: create quota change ticket (OBS-7123), wire in a short-lived flag in the collector, add metrics to the canary dashboard (Liam to own OBS-7123 follow-ups).

Runbook updates
- Add a new section 'heatmap-pruning' with steps to identify high-cardinality panels, archiving checklist, and ownership handoff template (Ritika to draft; due 2026-09-25).
- Add a canned rollback recipe for quota changes (includes Slack channel, pager oncalls, and exact API commands to revert collector config). Marcus will add the exact CLI commands and a one-liner to re-enable previous quota (due 2026-09-21).

Decisions made
- Proceed with quick wins immediately; schedule medium-term work for Sprint+1.
- Approve a 48h quota canary restricted to whitelist; platform will implement change early 2026-09-22 03:00 UTC (pre-window communication to GTM required).
- Add canary dashboard and attach to SLO alert runbook for auto-rollback.

Open questions and risks
- Will pre-aggregated percentiles match product QA expectations for fine-grained debugging? Need a short experiment comparing raw heatmap vs percentiles on 5 example tickets (Evan + Sofia, due 2026-09-30).
- Some internal teams rely on the cross-product heatmap to debug model-version regressions; archive path must include a discoverable link and a clear retrieval request process.
- Potential customer-facing impact if sampling excludes a noisy tenant; need to coordinate with Solutions Eng for customers in the whitelist.

Action items
- Marcus: run dashboard hit-counts and produce a CSV of candidates (due 2026-09-20).
- Liam: open/merge PR to reduce resolution for cpu hotspot tiles (PR #482, target merge 2026-09-22).
- Sofia: archive legacy heatmap into 'archive' folder and ping owners (done by 2026-09-24).
- Ritika: draft heatmap-pruning runbook section and link examples (2026-09-25).
- Evan + Sofia: run percentile vs heatmap experiment and write short note (2026-09-30).
- Platform (cc: platform-oncall): schedule quota canary and add canary dashboard widgets (OBS-7123 owner: Liam, due 2026-09-22).

Standup-style quick status (for next sync)
- Marcus: running inventory queries (in progress)
- Liam: PR in review
- Sofia: prepping archive
- Ritika: runbook skeleton in progress

Blockers
- Need signoff from Privacy/Legal on retaining archived heatmaps with user-level identifiers (task assigned to Lauren Chu, awaiting review).
- Platform team needs exact metric names to populate canary dashboard (Evan to provide list by 2026-09-20).

Notes-to-self
- Keep the initial canary conservative; prefer two sequential 48h windows rather than a single 96h run.
- Communicate changes in #observability with a short summary and links to the archive and runbook.

Appendix (quick links)
- Inventory doc (internal): DOC:heatmap-inventory-2026-09
- Quota ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-7123
- PR to reduce resolution: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482

Next meeting: follow-up sync 2026-09-25 09:30 PDT (15m) — agenda: inventory results, runbook draft review, canary readiness checklist
